node.label: Polity & Constitution
node.summary: Constitution, Parliament and State legislatures, elections, courts and party politics.

facts.plain: State Election Commissions are constitutional bodies under Art. 243K (panchayats) and Art. 243ZA (municipalities).

facts.plain: Andhra Pradesh: YSRCP chief Jagan Mohan Reddy accused the State Election Commission of complicity in urban local body poll rigging; repolls were ordered in only four booths.

facts.plain: SC (CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi) quashed the Rajasthan SEC's order barring civil-society voter awareness before panchayat polls: election bodies have no monopoly on voter awareness.

facts.plain: The ECI will allow judges to e-sign orders on ECINet for West Bengal's 19 appellate tribunals. Over 38 lakh voter cases are pending out of about 60 lakh 'doubtful' cases.

facts.plain: Amit Shah claimed SIR removed about 13 crore names: 4.25 crore registered twice, 3 crore dead, 1 crore duplicates, plus 3 crore he called 'infiltrators'. These are his claims.

facts.text: Editorial: unexplained SIR malpractices could subvert the popular will, and the ECI's silence hurts trust. It also warns against questioning a past election without proof.
facts.plain: Editorial: unexplained SIR malpractices could subvert the popular will, and the ECI's silence hurts trust. It also warns against questioning a past election without proof.

facts.text: JD(U) expelled Mokama MLA **Anant Singh** and his wife Neelam Devi for six years for opposing the party's candidate; the Assembly asked him to reply on revoking his membership.
facts.plain: JD(U) expelled Mokama MLA Anant Singh and his wife Neelam Devi for six years for opposing the party's candidate; the Assembly asked him to reply on revoking his membership.

facts.text: **Tenth Schedule**, para 2(2): an independent member who joins a party after election is disqualified. The Presiding Officer decides.
facts.plain: Tenth Schedule, para 2(2): an independent member who joins a party after election is disqualified. The Presiding Officer decides.

facts.text: Bihar: independent MLCs **Bansidhar Brajwasi** (Tirhut Graduates') and **Rahul Raj** (Saran Teachers') 'joined' the BJP on 31 Oct, then said they only offered support. **Jan Suraaj Party** asked Council Chairman **Ram Bachan Rai** to disqualify them.
facts.plain: Bihar: independent MLCs Bansidhar Brajwasi (Tirhut Graduates') and Rahul Raj (Saran Teachers') 'joined' the BJP on 31 Oct, then said they only offered support. Jan Suraaj Party asked Council Chairman Ram Bachan Rai to disqualify them.

facts.text: Three AAP leaders joined the BJP before Punjab's 2027 election: **Kunwar Vijay Pratap** (Amritsar North, ex-IPS), **Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra** (Sanour) and **Chetan Singh Jauramajra** (Samana).
facts.plain: Three AAP leaders joined the BJP before Punjab's 2027 election: Kunwar Vijay Pratap (Amritsar North, ex-IPS), Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra (Sanour) and Chetan Singh Jauramajra (Samana).

facts.text: Debate: supporters see a check on hasty laws and a voice for graduates and teachers; critics see a costly House for defeated leaders. The article says reform them or abolish them.
facts.plain: Debate: supporters see a check on hasty laws and a voice for graduates and teachers; critics see a costly House for defeated leaders. The article says reform them or abolish them.

facts.text: **Second ARC (2007)** suggested turning Councils into 'councils of local governments' elected only by local body members, to strengthen local self-government.
facts.plain: Second ARC (2007) suggested turning Councils into 'councils of local governments' elected only by local body members, to strengthen local self-government.

facts.text: Tamil Nadu's Council was abolished in **1986** (MGR as CM); a 2010 revival resolution was reversed in 2011. Andhra Pradesh's was abolished in **1985** (NTR) and re-created in **2007**.
facts.plain: Tamil Nadu's Council was abolished in 1986 (MGR as CM); a 2010 revival resolution was reversed in 2011. Andhra Pradesh's was abolished in 1985 (NTR) and re-created in 2007.

facts.text: The **Government of India Act, 1935** created bicameral legislatures in six provinces: Madras, Bombay, Bengal, United Provinces, Bihar, Assam. Members then served 9 years.
facts.plain: The Government of India Act, 1935 created bicameral legislatures in six provinces: Madras, Bombay, Bengal, United Provinces, Bihar, Assam. Members then served 9 years.

facts.text: Delay power comes from **Art. 197** (3 months, then 1 month on re-passage). On Money Bills the Council can only recommend (**Art. 198**, 14 days).
facts.plain: Delay power comes from Art. 197 (3 months, then 1 month on re-passage). On Money Bills the Council can only recommend (Art. 198, 14 days).

facts.text: Weak powers: no joint sitting, the Assembly's version prevails, and the Council can delay a bill by at most **four months**.
facts.plain: Weak powers: no joint sitting, the Assembly's version prevails, and the Council can delay a bill by at most four months.

facts.text: **Art. 172**: a permanent House, never dissolved. Members serve **6 years**; one-third retire every **2 years**. Ministers, including the CM, can be Council members.
facts.plain: Art. 172: a permanent House, never dissolved. Members serve 6 years; one-third retire every 2 years. Ministers, including the CM, can be Council members.

facts.text: **Art. 171**: Council strength at most **one-third** of the Assembly and at least **40**. Members: 1/3 elected by local bodies, 1/12 by graduates, 1/12 by teachers, 1/3 by MLAs, 1/6 nominated by the Governor.
facts.plain: Art. 171: Council strength at most one-third of the Assembly and at least 40. Members: 1/3 elected by local bodies, 1/12 by graduates, 1/12 by teachers, 1/3 by MLAs, 1/6 nominated by the Governor.

facts.text: **Art. 169**: Parliament creates or abolishes a Council by ordinary law, after the State Assembly passes a resolution by a **two-thirds majority**.
facts.plain: Art. 169: Parliament creates or abolishes a Council by ordinary law, after the State Assembly passes a resolution by a two-thirds majority.

facts.text: Six States have a Legislative Council: **Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka** (Art. 168). 28 Council seats were contested last week in UP, Bihar, Maharashtra and Karnataka.
facts.plain: Six States have a Legislative Council: Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka (Art. 168). 28 Council seats were contested last week in UP, Bihar, Maharashtra and Karnataka.
keys: Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka

facts.text: Right to protest vs preventive detention (Jantar Mantar rally stopped at Minto Road): Art. 19(1)(a) and (b) guarantee speech and peaceful assembly, subject to reasonable restrictions under Art. 19(2) and 19(3).
facts.plain: Right to protest vs preventive detention (Jantar Mantar rally stopped at Minto Road): Art. 19(1)(a) and (b) guarantee speech and peaceful assembly, subject to reasonable restrictions under Art. 19(2) and 19(3).

facts.text: Op-ed view: celebration is not an 'automatic licence' to expose others to health risks. Regulate with standards and accountability rather than choose between a blanket ban and a free-for-all.
facts.plain: Op-ed view: celebration is not an 'automatic licence' to expose others to health risks. Regulate with standards and accountability rather than choose between a blanket ban and a free-for-all.

facts.text: **Art. 48A** (Directive Principle) asks the State to protect the environment, forests and wildlife; **Art. 51A(g)** makes protecting the environment a Fundamental Duty.
facts.plain: Art. 48A (Directive Principle) asks the State to protect the environment, forests and wildlife; Art. 51A(g) makes protecting the environment a Fundamental Duty.

facts.text: The SC called cracker-bursting a religious practice for Deepavali but held that **Art. 25(1)** is a 'qualified' right, subject to public order, morality and health, and must be read with **Art. 21** (right to a healthy environment).
facts.plain: The SC called cracker-bursting a religious practice for Deepavali but held that Art. 25(1) is a 'qualified' right, subject to public order, morality and health, and must be read with Art. 21 (right to a healthy environment).

facts.text: CJI **Surya Kant** flagged litigants' 'growing tendency' to rush to the Supreme Court for early hearings even as **65,54,788 cases** remain pending in High Courts (25 High Courts face 292 judicial vacancies against a sanctioned strength of 1,122) and the Supreme Court's own backlog nears one lakh (97,201 cases).
facts.plain: CJI Surya Kant flagged litigants' 'growing tendency' to rush to the Supreme Court for early hearings even as 65,54,788 cases remain pending in High Courts (25 High Courts face 292 judicial vacancies against a sanctioned strength of 1,122) and the Supreme Court's own backlog nears one lakh (97,201 cases).

facts.text: West Bengal's government notified Group D government jobs for one family member of each person killed in political violence over the preceding 25 years (income cutoff ₹50,000/month), a day after CM Suvendu Adhikari's announcement in Paschim Medinipur.

facts.text: BJP president **Nitin Nabin** accused the Congress of 'protecting three crore infiltrators' during a 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' march in Rohtak on Haryana Foundation Day, countering the INDIA bloc's Ramlila Maidan rally over the SIR.

facts.text: Union Home Minister Amit Shah said Chandigarh will be India's first city to become drug-free; Chandigarh Police have achieved a **93% conviction rate** in NDPS Act cases since the new criminal laws took effect (8,206 FIRs registered since 4 August 2024).

facts.text: Andhra Pradesh held civic polls for 13 municipal corporations and 79 municipalities/nagar panchayats; overall turnout was **48.03%** (vs 63.30% in 2021), with Machilipatnam highest (55.10%) and Greater Visakhapatnam lowest (39.72%); YSRCP's Jagan Mohan Reddy demanded a repoll in Pulivendula alleging malpractice.

facts.text: **Article 44** (Directive Principle) asks the State to secure a Uniform Civil Code. **Uttarakhand** became the first State to implement a UCC on **27 Jan 2025**; **Goa** has had a common civil code since Portuguese rule.
